source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
3.3V rail (AXP2101 DCDC1, 2A) — this is the main power source whenever the power board is attached:
\- ESP32-S3 module
\- INA219
\- Every I2C sensor (SCD41, BME280, ENS160) through the sensor board
\- I2C display
\- TTP223, AM312 PIR

5V rail (MT3608 boost, 500mA) — ESP32 GPIO3 controls this rail:
\- SPS30 particulate sensor
\- ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
\- SK6812 LEDs (when connected to 5V — version-dependent)

3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — active only if the main board's USB-C is connected WITHOUT the power board:
\- It supplies the same 3.3V rail listed above. With Schottky diode OR-ing, whichever source is available takes precedence. This is for standalone programming.

Battery (3.7–4.2V) — supplies the AXP2101, which subsequently powers everything listed above.

The simple rule is that the AXP2101 supplies everything during normal operation. The LDO activates only for programming when the power board is not connected.

value_updates.battery_power_path: The battery supplies the AXP2101, which powers the system during normal operation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Great. What is your opinion of the [PASSWORD_001] Is there a simpler way to handle this? I need the battery to charge while the device is operating, and I also require 3.3V and 5V rails. If there is a better and simpler solution, please suggest it.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: However, it has to use the battery efficiently because the objective is to maximize battery life.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I mean, it is a good chip and provides exactly what I need, but it requires many static components, so I am uncertain. I know of TP4056 and similar chips, but I do not think they work as well when charging + powering simultaneously, and AXP also provides some advanced features.

ambiguity.description: The client is uncertain whether to retain the AXP2101 or adopt a simpler power-management solution while preserving simultaneous charging and operation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Alright, good; in that case, let’s keep it.
